rationale: Evidence fingerprint a8998eaa... and history fingerprint a4513fc3... match the decision. The held text and span hashes check out: EO_10773.txt ae4640e8..., EO_11051 FR text, and the APP 11051 mirror, with exact provision spans. Identity is confirmed: 23 FR 5061, July 1, 1958, 'Delegating and Transferring Certain Functions and Affairs to the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization'. The held original ends at '(Continued on p. 5063)' after sec. 4(b)(7), so sec. 7 (cross-referenced by sec. 2(b)) and the later sections are not held. The producer discloses this gap correctly. EO 11051 sec. 604 (27 FR, signed Sept. 27, 1962) reads 'To the extent that the following have not heretofore been made or become inapplicable, they are hereby superseded and revoked', listing '(9) Executive Order No. 10773 of July 1,1958'. The only savings parenthetical is on item (7), EO 10539. The cruden number search (19 hits) found amendments or partial actions only: EO 10782, 10838 (amends EO 10700 as amended by 10773), 10901/10902/10903 (cite 10773), 10941, 10952 sec. 7 (amends 10773 'accordingly'), and EO 10958 (supersedes prior orders including 10773 'to the extent' within its scope). None revives the order after 1962. The evidence therefore points to a whole-order end by EO 11051, which is a NO. The decision instead recommends 'yes' with no CURRENT predicate. That contradicts its own rationale and the review gate for YES, so the decision must be rejected however its prose reads. The single flag, PARTIAL_OR_QUALIFIED_CHANGE_REQUIRES_CLAUSE_CHECK, is explained for the amending orders. Its claim that sec. 604 carries 'no partial qualifier' sits uneasily with the cited ACT record's partial scope and 'to the extent' exceptions text, and that tension is not reconciled.

rationale: Evidence fingerprint 372fcbd0... and history fingerprint 3d99ddb6... match the decision. The held text hashes match: EO_10946.txt 380a6151... and EO_11374.txt 124f998e.... The ACT span (chars 2255-2318) reads exactly 'Executive Order No. 10946 of May 26, 1961, is hereby revoked.', with scope whole and no savings. Identity is confirmed: 26 FR 4629, May 26, 1961, 'Establishing a program for resolving labor disputes at missile and space sites'. I read both texts in full. EO 11374 (32 FR 14199, signed Oct. 11, 1967) contains no effective-date wording. Sec. 1 abolishes the Missile Sites Labor Commission and transfers its functions to FMCS. Secs. 2-5 provide continued priority procedures, agency cooperation, transfer of records and property, and resolution of pending disputes by the existing members on special assignment. Sec. 6 revokes EO 10946 without qualification. The producer describes all of this accurately and correctly declines to treat signing or publication as an effective date. The cruden search returned 4 hits (the original, EO 11374 FR, EO 11374 APP mirror, and the EO 11374 1989 text) and no later revival. The history has no flags, and the API and 1989 rows agree as editorial leads. The NO outcome is therefore well supported. However, the stated earlier-ending analysis is wrong: sec. 9's authority to pay Commission expenditures from the President's emergency fund is expressly limited to fiscal years 1961 and 1962. That is an own-terms partial end of that sub-authority (after June 30, 1962), and the producer denies that any command has one. The producer's mention of 'FY1961-62 fund provisions' among residual lifecycle questions does not cure the false affirmative statement. Under the strict rule that the reasons must be true, the decision is rejected. A corrected sheet that names the sec. 9 fiscal-year limit as a partial earlier lapse, leaving the whole-order end at EO 11374 sec. 6, would be acceptable.
